title: All Rome: only living, charity-formed faith actually justifies; Aquinas and Becanus
source_text: XVI. Sed hoc misso, fatentur Doctores omnes Ecclesiae Romanae fidem mortuam, & quae cum charitate juncta non est, ad salutem non prodesse, nec ad justitiam assequendam valere, neque fidem ullum actu servare & justificare, nisi quum viva est, & per dilectionem efficax. Haec est praesertim Thomae Aquinatis doctrina. Etenim negans fidem informem esse virtutem, fidem formatam virtutem esse probat, ex eo quod per illam justificamur, quia scilicet, non justificamur, nisi per illud quod habet rationem virtutis. 2. 2. Quaest. 4. art. 5. Idem vero post Thomam expresse docet Martinus Becanus Jesuita, eandemque sententiam omnibus suis Catholicis tribuit. Catholici, inquit, docent fidem non justificare, nisi sit formata charitate. Item, Catholici docent eam fidem posse informem existere, non tamen, nisi formatam justificare. In Summa Theologiae Scholasticae, tom. 2. tractatu 4. cap. 2. num. 7.
pass_a_gloss: But this being set aside, all the Doctors of the Roman Church confess that dead faith, and that which is not joined with charity, does not profit unto salvation, nor avail for obtaining justice, nor does any faith actually save and justify unless when it is living and effective through love. This is especially the doctrine of Thomas Aquinas. For denying that unformed faith is a virtue, he proves that formed faith is a virtue from this, that through it we are justified, because namely we are not justified except through that which has the nature of a virtue. 2.2. Question 4, article 5. And the same after Thomas Martin Becanus the Jesuit expressly teaches, and attributes the same sentence to all his Catholics. Catholics, he says, teach that faith does not justify unless it is formed by charity. Likewise, Catholics teach that that faith can exist unformed, yet not justify unless formed. In the Summa of Scholastic Theology, tom. 2, treatise 4, chapter 2, number 7.
pass_b_english: Setting the historical label aside: all Roman doctors confess dead faith without charity does not profit to salvation or justice, and no faith actually saves and justifies unless it is living and effective through love.
Aquinas: unformed faith is not a virtue; formed faith is, because we are justified only through what has the nature of a virtue.
Becanus for Catholics generally: faith can exist unformed, but justifies only when formed by charity.

lemmas.gloss: unless it is formed by charity
